questions.text: When everything around you starts falling apart, what is your first instinct?

options.text: Take responsibility and find a way forward, even if the burden falls on you.
Make sure everyone is safe and supported before anything else.
Step forward, organize people, and lead them through the crisis.
Look beyond the immediate problem and search for the deeper cause.

questions.text: When someone you barely know asks for your trust, how do you respond?

options.text: I remain cautious and look for signs of their true intentions.
I want to believe them, even when my own judgment tells me to be careful.
I observe their actions before deciding whether they deserve my trust.
I give them a chance, but I expect honesty and loyalty in return.

questions.text: What motivates you most when you set yourself a difficult goal?

options.text: The chance to accomplish something meaningful, even if it requires sacrifice.
The opportunity to prove that I am capable of more than others expect.
The desire to protect something or someone I deeply care about.
The satisfaction of achieving something together with people I trust.

questions.text: You must make an important decision, but you have very little information. What do you do?

options.text: Trust my instincts and take action rather than remain paralyzed.
Wait, observe, and gather as much information as possible.
Consider the consequences carefully and avoid unnecessary risks.
Choose the path that feels right, even if I cannot explain why.

questions.text: When someone strongly disagrees with you, what is your usual reaction?

options.text: I stay calm and try to understand the bigger picture.
I defend my position directly and refuse to back down easily.
I look for a solution that preserves everyone's dignity.
I try to understand what is really driving the disagreement.

questions.text: You are offered something you deeply desire, but accepting it could change who you are. What do you do?

options.text: Refuse it, even if giving it up is painful.
Think about whether I could use it responsibly for a greater purpose.
Consider whether the opportunity is too important to let go.
Question why I want it so badly and what it might cost me.

questions.text: When working with a group, which role comes most naturally to you?

options.text: The strategist who thinks several steps ahead.
The one who notices details others tend to overlook.
The dependable person who keeps everyone motivated.
The practical teammate who brings energy and determination.

questions.text: When something important goes wrong because of a decision you made, how do you react?

options.text: I accept responsibility and try to make things right.
I feel the weight of the failure, but I keep moving forward.
I analyze what happened so I can avoid the same mistake.
I focus on supporting the people affected by the situation.

questions.text: How do you feel when life forces you into an unfamiliar situation?

options.text: I adapt and take the opportunity to grow into something new.
I prefer to understand the situation before making any changes.
I resist losing what is familiar and important to me.
I feel conflicted, but eventually follow the path that seems necessary.

questions.text: If you were given a responsibility that could affect many people's lives, what would matter most to you?

options.text: Making the difficult decisions that others are unwilling to make.
Ensuring that nobody is abandoned along the way.
Using wisdom and experience to guide people toward the right direction.
Protecting what matters, even if the responsibility becomes a personal burden.
